I am furious and deeply upset about what happened to my dog at 21pooch in Downtown Los Angeles on September 5.

I brought my dog in for a 3:30 p.m. on the 5th of September 2026 for a grooming appointment with photographs showing the exact haircut and pattern I wanted. I was very specific.

After I left, I received a call saying there was some matting around his NECK and that they needed to cut that area a little shorter. There was NO matting on his head. I agreed only to the neck being cut a little shorter and made it clear that I did NOT want his coat taken very short. I was specifically assured that it would “definitely not” be skin-short.

I also gave one very clear instruction: DO NOT CUT HIS HEAD SHORTER.

I was told okay.

My phone automatically records incoming calls, so there is a record of exactly what was said.

When I returned around 5:20 p.m., I was horrified. What they had done was completely contrary to the photographs I brought and the instructions I gave both in person and over the phone.

This was not a misunderstanding, and it was not a situation where my dog was matted all over and they had no choice. The matting they called me about was around his neck. I gave limited permission to shorten that area. I specifically said not to take the rest of him too short and not to shorten his head.

They did it anyway.

What concerns me just as much is the conduct of the person at the front reception. At 21pooch, the receptionist receives the owner’s instructions and communicates them to the groomer. When I confronted them, she began claiming that I had said things online and during our phone conversation that I never said. Because my phone automatically records the calls, I know what was and was not said.

If you are the person standing between the owner and the groomer, you cannot decide which instructions to communicate, which to ignore, and then attribute statements to the owner that were never made.

When I asked to speak with the groomer who worked on my dog, the receptionist was also hesitant to bring the groomer out. That made me seriously question what the groomer had actually been told.

These are PEOPLE’S ANIMALS. They are family. A dog cannot defend himself or tell the groomer, “That is not what my owner asked you to do.” The process depends on the person receiving the owner’s instructions communicating them honestly and accurately.

Nothing is more important to me than my dog. I know his personality and how he reacts, which is exactly why I brought pictures and gave specific instructions.

Since coming home, he has been visibly unhappy and withdrawn and will barely look at me. My apartment also gets extremely cold, which was another reason I did not want his coat taken this short.

I have respected 21pooch in the past because of how they treated my dogs, but this experience has completely damaged that trust.

If an owner provides photographs, gives explicit instructions, repeats those instructions during a phone call, and is assured they will be followed, those instructions need to be followed.

I even asked explicitly for them not to cut the tail but they still did it anyways. And mind you the tail was not mated. The hair on the legs are uneven it's been a couple of weeks I'm still waiting for it to even out

This was not just a bad haircut. It was a complete breakdown of trust.

I had a very disappointing experience with 21Pooch and unfortunately will not be returning.

I scheduled an appointment for my dog to receive a bath and dropped her off without any issues. About 15 minutes later, I received a call saying they were unable to handle her and that I needed to come pick her up. While I understand that not every groomer will be able to work with every dog, what I found completely unreasonable was being told that I would still be charged the FULL price of the service, despite the fact that the service was not performed.

I pushed back because I could not find any clearly disclosed policy during the booking process stating that customers would be charged the full service price if the staff determined they could not handle their dog. It also did not make sense to me to charge the full amount for a bath that was never completed, particularly when they still had appointment availability that day.

After I expressed my concerns, they did reduce the charge. I appreciate that they were willing to make an adjustment, but I still disagree with being charged at all for a service that was not performed.

What bothered me most was how the situation was handled. If there is a handling, cancellation, or unsuccessful-service fee in situations like this, it should be clearly and explicitly disclosed on the website and during the booking process so customers can make an informed decision before leaving their pets.

They told me they hoped I would return, but unfortunately this experience left a very negative impression. I expected better customer service and a more reasonable approach to resolving the situation. I will be taking my dog elsewhere in the future.

Their online registration booking system isn’t working, called to do it manually, then I was told that isn’t possible and that the only way to book is through the online booking system (stuck between a rock and hard place I guess) and was told if there’s anything else I need with I should call. Very passive aggressive considering that the receptionist literally has one job, manage bookings and client issues.

Brought my beloved 18lb senior dog in for a quick nail trim while passing by on our walk. She took him to the back and that’s when I heard my dog yelp. The receptionist checked on him and said it was another dog, but I know what my dog sounds like. Frankie was in the back for a simple nail trim for 15 minutes and when he was returned to me he was panicked and panting; this is when I was told they flipped him upside down to trim the hair on his feet. I only took him here out of convenience because I live down the street; I usually take him to a petsmart in Hollywood. I have had this dog for ten years. He is an easy dog. I have seen him get his nails done time and time again with no issue I and did them myself with an emery board during Covid. To flip my dog upside down was unacceptable. I regret walking in here and I regret paying them any money for traumatizing my dog. The groomer should not have a job working with dogs. This was at 11:45am on July 9th.

On July 6, 2025, I booked a same-day 3:30 PM appointment for my dog's haircut and bath, expecting professional grooming. Shockingly, upon arrival, the groomer said they couldn't provide the haircut--the primary service I booked--and instead pushed dematting and a bath for an outrageous $130, $80 of that specifically for a dematting fee. As a diligent pet owner who brushes my dog every three days, I was stunned, as my poodle mix gets washed and brushed at home regularly, making this fee completely unjustified when he should only have minor matting if any. When I declined the unnecessary services and wanted to cancel due to their inability to provide the haircut, they hit me with a 50% cancellation fee. This felt like a blatant money-grab, with no mention of these exorbitant fees or service limitations when I booked. The lack of transparency and predatory pricing is unacceptable. I left feeling exploited and pressured into a $130 bath and will never return. Pet owners, especially poodle owners beware of these shady tactics--take your business to a trustworthy groomer or Petco, where you can wash your dog yourself for a fraction of the cost.
